content: While taking this medication, you may experience changes in body fat distribution, such as an increase in fat around the upper back and stomach areas, and a decrease in fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not yet fully understood. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. This document does not list all possible side effects, so it is important to consult your healthcare provider for medical advice regarding any concerns. Before starting nelfinavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. If you are pregnant, discuss the use of this medication with your doctor, as it can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. However, this medication passes into breast milk and may harm a nursing infant. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication, as breast milk can also transmit HIV. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Nelfinavir can slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. Similarly, other medications may impact how nelfinavir works. Examples of interacting drugs include apalutamide, certain anti-seizure medications (such as carbamazepine, phenobarbital, and primidone), and rifampin. Additionally, this medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods like pills, patches, or rings, which could result in pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Regular lab and medical tests, such as liver function, viral load, T-cell counts, triglycerides/cholesterol, and blood sugar levels, should be conducted while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
